audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer graded this FAV at 4/10 difficulty with a "Free harass lane" TL;DR and a 5/10 carry threat, while the content layer on the same page calls the late game unwinnable and hands Cho'Gath four of seven stages. Level 3, First item and 2+ items also carried Akshan-favoured why text under a Cho'Gath side.
audit.why: Akshan's packet win rate here is 33.33% over 21 games — the worst in the slice. Cho'Gath's Feral Scream (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s) silences Heroic Swing, which is Akshan's only exit, and permanent Feast health makes physical poke decay every minute. Nothing about that is a free lane.
audit.corrected: Difficulty regraded to HARD 8/10 with an 8/10 carry threat, and the three contradicted stages rewritten so the why matches its own side: silence at 3, Feast stacks outgrowing Youmuu's at first item, and a rounding-error poke bar at two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was marked Akshan in both the content win array and the full phases, but the same page's whys[4] says Feast kills you at 6 before Comeuppance finishes channeling.
audit.why: Comeuppance (100/85/70) has to store bullets before it fires; Feast (80/70/60) is instant on cast. Both cannot own level 6, and the page's own text says Cho'Gath does.
audit.corrected: Level 6 flipped to Cho'Gath in both layers with a why that states the channel-versus-instant race. Flagged as force-length because a side field cannot change words without leaving the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feast (R) is described in five places as "a true-damage percent-missing-HP execute" with a "threshold" you drop below. It is not. Riot's description is "Devours an enemy unit, dealing a high amount of true damage" — a flat lump, no missing-health scaling, no execute threshold. Separately, dosFull[2] called Rupture a "fifteen-second invitation" and the whole page treated the knockup as the ability to fear.
audit.why: The threshold framing tells you that staying above some HP percentage makes you safe, which is false and will get people killed. Rupture is a flat 6s cooldown, so it is not a punishable window at all — Feral Scream at 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s is, and it is the ability that actually beats Akshan because a silence stops Heroic Swing from being cast.
audit.corrected: Feast is now a lump of true damage that ignores armour and the Dirty Fighting shield; Rupture is stated at its real flat 6s; and the tracked ability across cooldowns, do's, don'ts, loading and the interactions report is switched to Feral Scream's 11s silence.

Rupture is a flat 6s, so treat it as constant and sidestep rather than wait it out. The instant he hits 6 everything inverts: Feast (R) is a lump of true damage that ignores armour and the shield from your third Dirty Fighting stack, and it resolves instantly while your own R (Comeuppance) still has to store bullets. Respect that: never duel a Cho'Gath holding Feast, no matter how far ahead your early trades looked.

notes: Feast was described as a percent-missing-health execute with a threshold in five separate strings across both layers — Riot's description is a flat lump of true damage, so every instance was corrected. That framing was actively dangerous: it implied staying above some HP percentage made you safe. Two side-field edits (full phases[4].side and content win[4]) cannot stay inside the +/-10% length band because a side value is a single word; both are included and flagged. MC_WR_TABLES value disagrees with the packet's 33.33% over 21 games and was not touched.
